conditions_met_evidence: No argument: describes the sunk cost effect and reports a study.
notes: Teaching/reporting; entry mentioned: sunk-cost.

error_sentence: So coffee with it is probably fine, though I'll confirm at my next refill.
conditions_met_evidence: C3 of argument-from-ignorance fails: the full interactions list and the manufacturer's checker are places where a caffeine interaction would be expected.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'thorough search was done' applies; conclusion hedged ('probably') and checked later.

error_sentence: So roughly 9% of restaurants ... probably have lapsed certificates
conditions_met_evidence: Random sample of 1,200, conclusion hedged with error band; C3 of hasty-generalization fails; C2 of unrepresentative-sample fails (random sample).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Tentative conclusion with appropriate caution.

error_sentence: that money is gone whatever we decide. Looking only forward ...
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: past cost explicitly set aside; decision rests on future costs/revenue.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Real remaining benefit.
notes: Correct handling of sunk cost.

error_sentence: seems, I freely confess, absurd ... can hardly be considered real.
conditions_met_evidence: C2 fails: speaker states incredulity and then rejects it as a reason, giving conditions (gradations, variation, inheritance).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Speaker identifies and rebuts the incredulity move (METHOD g).
notes: Darwin, Origin of Species ch. 6 (historical). Correct rebuttal.

error_sentence: But that result tells you nothing, because dowsing doesn't work when skeptics are watching; their doubt interferes with the signal.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 claim (dowsing works) faces counterevidence: 11/50 vs ~10 by chance. C2 extra assumption: skeptics' doubt interferes. C3 no independent reason given; offered as settling ('tells you nothing').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Rescuing assumption has no independent support in text. Unfalsifiability considered: same family, one label; ad hoc rescue fits the specific unsupported assumption.

error_sentence: The trial was also run on a Tuesday, and groundwater signals are always weak early in the week.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 same counterevidence. C2 second invented assumption (weak Tuesday signals). C3 no support given; offered as further excuse.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No independent support stated.
notes: Separate second rescue, separate assumption; recorded as its own error.

error_sentence: if the county thinks dowsing is useless, it's up to the county to prove that.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 claim: dowsing works/reliable. C2 claimant says others must disprove it. C3 claimant's only evidence (the trial) is null; no support given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Asking someone to support their own claim' does not apply (the county isn't the claimant); 'after a real case has been made' does not apply (no case made).
notes: Same family as next row; treated as a separate move (burden demand) from the conclusion drawn in the next sentence.

error_sentence: Until someone demonstrates that it can't work, we're entitled to keep advertising it as reliable.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 not proven false. C2 concluded 'reliable' (true) on that basis. C3 no thorough search showing it works; the only test came out at chance.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Procedural default LA does not apply: no independent rule, and an established standard (the controlled trial) points the other way; not a precautionary decision.
notes: Last sentence ('prices will stay the same') is irrelevant filler, no inference.

error_sentence: "The market punished the airline" just means investors sold its shares
conditions_met_evidence: Reification C2 fails: the abstraction is explicitly unpacked into investors' actions; conclusion limited.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Shorthand unpacked without changing conclusion.
notes: Contrast with R051.

error_sentence: the point of the rule is to let people work undisturbed, not to stop anyone getting help in an emergency
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker correctly applies the rule's rationale to the exception.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Correct exception handling.
notes: Contrast with R076.

error_sentence: But let's be clear: the company failed because of the finance chief. Had he reported honestly, it would still be here.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 outcome attributed to one cause ('because of the finance chief'). C2 other causes named in the same passage: recession cutting demand 30%, failed launch, rising interest. C3 counterfactual 'it would still be here' relies on his conduct being the whole story.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Picking the most important cause while acknowledging others' does not apply: the others are listed then dismissed ('let's be clear').

error_sentence: But abandoning it now would mean all that money was wasted, so we have to finish it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 choice about what to do next. C2 $4.2M and three years cited. C3 treated as the reason to continue, while the future-looking evidence (loses money every year; bus serves more riders) points the other way.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No evidence about prospects (forecast is negative); no trust/reputation reason; no remaining benefit or switching cost stated.

error_sentence: the rule exists to prevent harm, and a few seconds' delay for an emergency vehicle can cost a life
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: a reason relevant to the rule's purpose is given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Relevant difference stated and supported.

error_sentence: But even if the court finds there was a contract, my client did not breach it, and even if there was a breach...
conditions_met_evidence: Kettle logic C2 arguably met, but LA applies.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Arguing in the alternative, explicitly 'even if', each ground stated as separate.

error_sentence: Things like patient dignity or whether families felt informed can't be quantified, so they shouldn't factor into funding at all.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 funding based solely on discharges per bed per month. C2 (outside-text) dignity and whether families are informed are important to the goal of patient care: common knowledge, and the speaker names them. C3 dismissed explicitly because they 'can't be quantified'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Measured thing is what matters' fails: discharge speed is not patient outcome; the agency's survival measure in the same passage is not used.
notes: First half (state agency rating) is legitimate expertise, no issue. Entry is status contested (noted per METHOD).

error_sentence: Given the payment and the contradiction, the jury has good reason to give his testimony little weight.
conditions_met_evidence: Claim rests on the witness's word; conclusion limited to weight of testimony.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Questioning a witness's reliability when the claim rests on testimony; stake as reason to check.

error_sentence: But people would still get hit, so the signal isn't a real solution and we shouldn't install it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 proposal criticised. C2 criticism: doesn't solve whole problem ('people would still get hit'). C3 rejected without comparing to alternatives; a ~50% injury cut is set aside.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Situation does not require perfection.

error_sentence: It's the newest system on the market, so its risk scores must be more accurate
conditions_met_evidence: C1 said to be more accurate. C2 the only reason given is newness.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No evidence of real improvement given (contrast R074).

error_sentence: I never borrowed your ladder in the first place. Besides, one of the rungs was already cracked when you lent it to me. And anyway, I gave it back in perfect condition
conditions_met_evidence: C1 three defences for one conclusion. C2 'never borrowed' contradicts 'when you lent it to me' and 'gave it back'; 'already cracked' contradicts 'perfect condition'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not explicit arguing in the alternative ('even if'); stated as facts.

error_sentence: the procurement law requires that the same waiver be offered to every builder who asks
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: binding mechanism (procurement law) shown; hedged 'very likely'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Well-supported chain; binding mechanism LA.

error_sentence: He kept a logbook to prove it, then lost the logbook in a rainstorm, which he considered the final proof.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument by the speaker: humorous anecdote reporting grandfather's belief; the punchline signals non-endorsement.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Reports/satirises someone else's reasoning (METHOD g).
notes: Judgment call: treated as a joke. If the grandfather's reasoning were scored, it would be superstitious-thinking (or post-hoc). See NOTES.

error_sentence: So everyone on the maintenance crew has passed a safety exam.
conditions_met_evidence: Valid Barbara syllogism (All E are S; all M are E; so all M are S).
notes: Contrast with R095.

error_sentence: the phrase parent or mother country hath been jesuitically adopted by the king and his parasites, with a low papistical design
conditions_met_evidence: Appeal-to-motive C3 fails: the motive claim comes after two independent replies ('the more shame upon her conduct'; 'it happens not to be true, or only partly so'), so it is not offered in place of reasons.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Openly evaluative pamphlet (loaded-language LA); motive explanation after independent rebuttal.
notes: Paine, Common Sense (historical). Practical note: 'not true, or only partly so' is unsupported within the excerpt (Paine argues it later); and 'jesuitically/papistical' is anti-Catholic loaded wording - charged wording, not a second error.

error_sentence: Nowhere does it mention the cholera outbreak ... So the outbreak never reached the village, and the county records are wrong.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 diary doesn't mention outbreak. C2 concluded it didn't happen. C3 (outside-text) settled by the text: diary 'survives only in fragments' and remaining pages 'deal almost entirely with baptisms and pew rents', so no strong reason to expect a mention.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Source would very likely have mentioned it' fails (contrast R036, R043). Also overrides positive evidence (county records).

error_sentence: Someone who has given up everything has no reason to lie, so his prediction that the river will flood next Tuesday must be true.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 poverty cited ('owns nothing but the clothes on his back'). C2 offered as the reason his prediction is true; predicting a flood is unrelated to money, and sincerity does not make a prediction accurate.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Cheapness-tracks-value LA irrelevant.
notes: Also: honesty != accuracy (a sincere predictor can be wrong) - part of the same step.

error_sentence: that tank tested positive for bacterial contamination before filling
conditions_met_evidence: Division LA applies: contamination of the shared source carries down to each vial; conclusion is precautionary ('treated as contaminated until tested').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Property that carries down to every member.

error_sentence: I'll be voting on my brother-in-law's development, though, because I know I can be impartial, and the rule is really meant for people who can't be.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 rule accepted ('basic integrity'). C2 exception for self. C3 the reason given is self-assessed impartiality, which the recusal rule exists precisely to replace; not a reason relevant to the rule's purpose.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No relevant, supported difference: self-assessment is unsupported. Double-standard LA routes self-exemption here.
notes: Interpretation: treated 'I know I can be impartial' as not a purpose-relevant reason (a recusal rule removes self-judgment). Logged in NOTES.

error_sentence: The Vienna Philharmonic is one of the finest orchestras in the world. Our new neighbor plays in its viola section, so she must be one of the finest violists in the world
conditions_met_evidence: C1 whole's property (finest orchestra). C2 member concluded to have it. C3 no reason given why it carries over.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Property not definitional of membership.
notes: Second step ('her lessons will be the best in town') is a further leap (fine player -> best teacher), not separately rowed; see NOTES.

error_sentence: not because the claim has been proven false, but because it hasn't been shown to be true
conditions_met_evidence: Burden placed on claimant; conclusion limited to a regulatory decision, explicitly not 'false'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Procedural default LA; asking claimant to support own claim.

error_sentence: he had no right to believe on such evidence as was before him
conditions_met_evidence: Moral argument about responsibility for belief; no condition of any catalog entry met.
notes: Clifford, 'The Ethics of Belief' (historical).

error_sentence: If the forecaster knows that tomorrow's launch will be scrubbed, then the launch will necessarily be scrubbed. ... So the scrub is necessary, and nothing the engineers do tonight could change it
conditions_met_evidence: C1 conditional true by definition (knowledge entails truth). C2 'she knows' is merely true (and only via 'her models are excellent'). C3 scrub concluded necessary; 'nothing ... could change it'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: P not shown necessary.
notes: Also weak: 'models are excellent' -> 'she knows' (excellent models don't guarantee knowledge); not separately rowed.

error_sentence: We've put eight years and $30 million into the current scheduling system. Management: Switching now would throw all of that away, so we're keeping it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 choice to keep/switch. C2 past costs cited. C3 treated as the reason to continue; the union's stated future costs ($4M/yr vs $1.5M; error time 40 -> 5 min) are not addressed.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No trust/reputation reason; no remaining benefit or switching cost given by management.
notes: Committed by Management; Union representative's reply is a correct forward-looking rebuttal (no issue).

error_sentence: If that is acceptable for them, there is no good reason pharmacies shouldn't hand out high-dose morphine to anyone who asks.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 hospice patients vs anyone. C2 conclusion carried across. C3 relevant difference: terminal illness/palliative supervision, where addiction and overdose risks are weighed differently (common knowledge).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Shared feature (asking for morphine) is not what matters to the conclusion; not an illustration.

conditions_met_evidence: No argument: obituary.

error_sentence: A genuine charity, properly understood, is one that spends nothing at all on salaries or advertising.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 'charity' narrowed far beyond ordinary meaning. C2 builds in contested evaluation (overhead = not genuine). C3 presented as 'properly understood' and the conclusion depends on it.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not an announced technical stipulation (contrast R068); not argued for openly.
notes: First thought: no true Scotsman. Family rule: no counterexample is redefined on the spot, the definition comes first, so persuasive definition.

conditions_met_evidence: No argument: meeting minutes.

error_sentence: So we'll keep it as one input, and also sample fifty tickets per agent ...
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: the hard-to-measure factor is explicitly included.
notes: Contrast with R091.

error_sentence: But Mill Street can't have been named for a mill; "mill" comes from the Latin molina, a place for grinding grain, and there was never any grinding here, only a sawmill.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 origin cited (molina). C2 offered as the real meaning. C3 current usage differs: a sawmill is a mill (common knowledge); argument relies on old meaning.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not merely explaining how a meaning arose.
notes: Committed by Member. Archivist's argument from silence is legitimate (complete minutes recording every renaming) - no issue.

error_sentence: So the name must honor some family called Mill.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 two origins treated as exhaustive (mill vs family named Mill). C2 other options exist: named for the sawmill (once the etymology error is removed), a miller, a person not named Mill, a transferred name. C3 'must' relies on eliminating the mill option.
lookalikes_ruled_out: True dichotomy LA fails.
notes: Possible issue rather than flag because this step's failure largely inherits the etymological error; could be read as one step. Settled by whether reviewers treat 'must honor a family' as a separate inference.

error_sentence: So cutting back is well supported even while the exact target is debated.
conditions_met_evidence: Inflation-of-conflict C2 fails: conclusion is limited to the point on which experts agree.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Concluding the specific disputed point is unsettled.
notes: Contrast with R081.

error_sentence: That gap, not the raw improvement, is the program's estimated effect.
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: regression explicitly considered; randomized comparison.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Comparison group LA applies.
notes: Contrast with R100.

error_sentence: mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person
conditions_met_evidence: No fallacy; argues against counting numbers as justification.
notes: J. S. Mill, On Liberty ch. 2 (historical).

error_sentence: Yet the council's landlord-lobby lapdogs, bought and paid for by greedy real-estate barons, voted it down.
conditions_met_evidence: Ad hominem C1/C3 fail: no opposing argument is stated, and the insult is not offered as a reason against one; the speaker argues the merits (38% vs 9%, cost 1.5%, reserve fund).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Insult not offered as a reason (ad-hominem LA); openly evaluative writing (loaded-language LA).
notes: Judgment call: rude and an unsupported corruption allegation, but no inference rests on it. See NOTES (could be scored possible issue by a stricter reviewer).

error_sentence: The only proof capable of being given that an object is visible, is that people actually see it. ... the sole evidence it is possible to produce that anything is desirable, is that people do actually desire it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 'visible'/'desirable' parallel. C2 possibly two senses: 'able to be seen' vs 'worth desiring'. C3 depends on reading: if Mill claims desire is evidence (not definition) of desirability, conclusion does not need the conflation.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Text supports a strongest reading where 'desire is the sole evidence of desirability' is a substantive evidential premise, so the equivocation is not shown from the words alone.
notes: Mill, Utilitarianism ch. 4 (historical). Moore's classic charge; contested in scholarship. Settled by whether 'desirable' is read as 'capable of being desired' in the analogy.

error_sentence: each person's happiness is a good to that person, and the general happiness, therefore, a good to the aggregate of all persons
conditions_met_evidence: C1 property of each part (happiness good to each). C2 whole concluded to have it ('good to the aggregate'). C3 no reason given in the passage for carryover.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Additive-property LA may apply if 'good to the aggregate' means 'the sum of goods'; the word 'aggregate' supports that reading, so not flagged.
notes: Settled by whether 'good' is read as additive (sum of each person's good) or as 'desired by the aggregate' as a single desirer.

error_sentence: There is something fascinating about science. One gets such wholesale returns of conjecture out of such a trifling investment of fact.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument by the author: satire of linear extrapolation; the last two sentences make the irony explicit.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Satirises a fallacy (METHOD g).
notes: Twain, Life on the Mississippi (historical). Entry satirised: over-extrapolation.

error_sentence: records every arrival and departure ... no gaps in its dates
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: source would very likely have mentioned the brig; hedged 'probably'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Source-would-mention LA.

error_sentence: the threat of death to me, to extort my money, and the threat of destruction to the Union, to extort my vote, can scarcely be distinguished in principle
conditions_met_evidence: False-analogy C3 fails: the shared features (threat to extort what is one's own, and blaming the victim for the threatened harm) are what matter to the conclusion about blame.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Analogy on relevant features.
notes: Lincoln, Cooper Union address (historical).

error_sentence: The word "nice" comes from the Latin nescius, meaning "ignorant." So when my editor called my essay "nice," she was really calling it ignorant
conditions_met_evidence: C1 origin cited. C2 offered as real meaning ('really calling it'). C3 current meaning (pleasant/good) differs; argument relies on old meaning.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not explanation of meaning history.

error_sentence: The chloroform temporarily allays the cough, thereby checking Nature's effort to throw off the dead matter from the lungs.
conditions_met_evidence: Argument from stated ingredients (morphine, chloroform) and a stated physiological mechanism; appeal-to-nature C3 fails (the 'Nature's effort' is a specific physiological function, coughing to clear lungs).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Physiological-evidence LA; sarcasm ('strike terror ... except the undertakers') follows a substantive reason, not in place of one.
notes: Samuel Hopkins Adams, The Great American Fraud (historical). Period medical claims may be dated; not a reasoning error.

error_sentence: your theory is confined to that which is seen; it takes no account of that which is not seen
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker correctly identifies and rebuts a fallacy (opportunity cost ignored).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Correct identification (METHOD g).
notes: Bastiat, 'That Which Is Seen' (historical). Catalog has no broken-window / seen-and-unseen entry; see NOTES.

error_sentence: The Extension.--This consists in carrying your opponent's proposition beyond its natural limits
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: describes a stratagem (straw man by extension) and its defence.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Teaching (METHOD g).
notes: Schopenhauer, Art of Controversy (historical).

error_sentence: He built three companies and is worth over a billion dollars. So when he says the city's bridge inspections are a waste of money, he's obviously right; you don't get that rich by being wrong.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 wealth cited. C2 offered as the reason his view is right ('you don't get that rich by being wrong'); whether bridge inspections are worthwhile is a public-safety/engineering question unrelated to his wealth.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Price-tracks-quality LA irrelevant.
notes: Appeal-to-accomplishment also fits (business achievements, different field). Family rule: money -> appeal to wealth; the stated warrant is wealth. C2 'unrelated to money' read as unrelated to his money-making; 'waste of money' does not make it a money question in the relevant respect.

error_sentence: The exit poll interviewed 3,100 individual voters
conditions_met_evidence: C3 fails: individual-level data.
notes: Contrast with R058.

error_sentence: because the Market is wiser than any of us and has no agenda, whatever it decides about the merger will by definition be the right outcome.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 'the Market' punishes, is wise, decides. C2 conclusion (the outcome is right) depends on taking the Market literally as a wise, agenda-free agent.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not unpackable shorthand: unpacking to 'investors trading shares' removes the conclusion (contrast R007).
notes: 'by definition be the right outcome' also verges on begging the question; not separately rowed (same step).

conditions_met_evidence: No argument: explains Simpson's paradox.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Teaching.

error_sentence: So you're saying we should deny people a drug that prevents strokes. ... I can't support a policy of letting patients have strokes to avoid a little dizziness.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 Osei's position restated. C2 differs materially: original is 'offering to high-risk patients rather than prescribing it routinely to everyone' (quoted in text). C3 Brandt attacks the restatement. C4 presented as rejecting Osei's policy.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not words Osei accepts (she explicitly rejects them); not a consequence she is committed to.
notes: Committed by Dr. Brandt. 'a little dizziness' also minimises the stated doubled severe-dizziness rate; same step.

error_sentence: Maya can live off campus, and Maya can hold a paid job. So under the terms she can live off campus and hold a paid job at the same time.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 'can A' and 'can B' (true in the divided sense under 'either ... or') read in the combined sense 'can (A and B)'. C2 the combined reading is the conclusion.
notes: Catalog's own example ('carry a tune and a piano') matches the pattern. Considered scope-fallacy/modal-scope: those concern 'necessarily'/'not'; combination of words is the closer fit. Noted in NOTES: no modern-name entry for 'possibly A, possibly B, so possibly A and B'.

error_sentence: the man who has fed the chicken every day ... at last wrings its neck
conditions_met_evidence: No argument committed: Russell illustrates the problem of induction.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Teaching.
notes: Russell, Problems of Philosophy ch. 6 (historical).

error_sentence: She clearly put the stress on this medication, which means she was telling me other medications are fine with alcohol. So a glass of wine with my sleeping pills tonight is no problem.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 meaning of the warning shifts with stress on 'this medication'. C2 conclusion relies on the shifted, contrastive meaning. C3 a pharmacist's interaction warning does not certify all other drugs safe with alcohol (common knowledge, esp. sleeping pills).
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Emphasis reflects what the speaker meant' fails: even if stressed, stress cannot mean 'other medications are fine'.
notes: Practical call: C3 met via common knowledge. Ambiguous whether the sleeping pills are 'this medication'; either way the inference fails.

error_sentence: The board minutes show the memos were discussed and then tabled.
conditions_met_evidence: Documented knowledge and inaction; no condition of a fallacy met.

error_sentence: Across the county's 140 precincts, the ones with the highest rates of boat ownership showed the lowest support ... That settles it: boat owners voted against the marina tax.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 precinct-level data. C2 conclusion about individual boat owners. C3 stated as settled ('That settles it') without individual-level data.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not used as a clue; no individual data (contrast R050).

error_sentence: Every child in the mentoring program has an adult who checks on them weekly. So there is an adult in the program who checks on every child weekly
conditions_met_evidence: C1 for every child some adult. C2 one adult for every child. C3 nothing else supports a single adult.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No separate evidence of a shared adult.

error_sentence: The next game we played far better, so punishment clearly works, and I'll do it after every bad game.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 (outside-text, settled by text) extreme result: 22% vs 36% season average, 'worst game of the season', followed by a better game. C2 sprints credited. C3 drift to average not considered by the coach.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No comparison group.
notes: Committed by Coach; Analyst correctly rebuts (no issue). Hasty generalization from one game is part of the same step.

error_sentence: following that expert consensus is reasonable
conditions_met_evidence: Appeal-to-authority C2 fails: genuine experts in field, broad agreement, backed by large studies.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Genuine expert consensus.

error_sentence: Rex only barks out in the yard and has never bitten anyone indoors, so he is not a dog that barks or bites in the unit.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 grammar ambiguity: does 'in the unit' modify 'bark' and 'bite' or only 'bite'? C2 argument relies on the wide-scope reading. C3 not shown: nothing in the passage shows the landlord meant the other reading.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Only one reading plausible' fails (both plausible).
notes: Settled by the rest of the lease or the drafter's intent (compare R083, where clause 2 resolves it). Tenant does not acknowledge the ambiguity.

error_sentence: For the rest, nothing is more ridiculous than the virtuous indignation of our bourgeois at the community of women ... The Communists have no need to introduce community of women; it has existed almost from time immemorial.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 bourgeois criticism (Communists would introduce community of women). C2 implied that the bourgeois already practise it ('virtuous indignation'; 'existed from time immemorial'); the hypocrisy is implied, not shown, in this excerpt. C3 partly: offered as dismissal ('ridiculous').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not flagged: the excerpt also gives a substantive rebuttal first (the real aim is ending women's status as instruments of production), so the jab is not the only reply. The earlier psychological explanation ('the bourgeois sees in his wife a mere instrument') was checked as bulverism: LA applies (the view is rebutted on its own terms).
notes: Marx and Engels, Communist Manifesto ch. 2 (historical). Settled by whether the following text (bourgeois adultery/prostitution) is used as the reason the objection fails.

error_sentence: a single master key that opens every office door ... So for each office ... there is at least one key that opens it
conditions_met_evidence: Valid direction (exists-forall to forall-exists).

error_sentence: The slaveholders themselves acknowledge it in the enactment of laws for their government.
conditions_met_evidence: Argument from opponents' own commitments (their laws).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Ad hominem LA: opponents' own stated commitments.
notes: Frederick Douglass, 'What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July?' (historical).

error_sentence: The flood-frequency methods used to estimate a hundred-year flood weren't developed until the 1930s, but any competent engineer would still have seen it coming. So they were negligent.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 1912 design decision judged. C2 (outside-text, settled by text) the methods were not available until the 1930s and 1927 is used as evidence ('just look at what happened in 1927').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not judged by what they knew at the time.

error_sentence: In no instance hath nature made the satellite larger than its primary planet, and as England and America ... reverses the common order of nature, it is evident they belong to different systems
conditions_met_evidence: C1 planet/satellite vs England/America. C2 political conclusion carried across ('it is evident'). C3 relevant difference: political governance does not depend on relative land size the way orbital relations depend on mass.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not an illustration: 'it is evident' relies on it.
notes: Paine, Common Sense (historical). Appeal-to-nature also arguable ('common order of nature'); chose false analogy because the inference is carried across from astronomy. Rhetoric in a persuasive pamphlet; a stricter charity reading could call it illustration.

error_sentence: For this report, we define a "high-overhead charity" as one that spends more than 35%
conditions_met_evidence: Stipulated, announced, sourced definition; disclaims evaluation.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Stipulated technical definition LA.
notes: Contrast with R033.

error_sentence: Since nothing else of importance favors Filter A, the city should choose Filter B.
conditions_met_evidence: Two options named without claiming exhaustiveness; comparison is complete for the stated choice.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Main-options LA.

error_sentence: My result came back positive, so there's a 95% chance I have it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 probability for a specific case from a test result. C2 (outside-text, settled by text) base rate stated: 1 in 1,000. C3 ignored: the positive predictive value is about 2% (0.99 / (0.99 + 49.95) per 1,000 tested).
lookalikes_ruled_out: Base rate not unknown; specific evidence not overwhelming.
notes: Probability family rule: test result read as chance of having condition -> base-rate. Booking the biopsy is reasonable and not an error.

error_sentence: That doesn't make it necessary that Dana married
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker correctly avoids the modal scope fallacy.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Correct use (METHOD g).

error_sentence: But this is just another power grab by unelected bureaucrats who despise rural people and want to drive family farmers off their land.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 the agency has put forward a rule (with an implied rationale). C2 reply attributes motives (power grab, despise rural people, want to drive farmers off). C3 'But this is just ...' offered in place of the merits the speaker admitted ('deserves serious debate').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Motives as reason to check word-based claims: the rule's cost figure is the agency's own estimate, not trusted testimony.
notes: C1 read as 'proposal counts as an argument' - logged in NOTES. First two sentences are sound.

error_sentence: Once this rule passes, next they'll be metering every garden hose in the state.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 rule opposed. C2 leads to metering every garden hose. C3 no reason given for the step; each later step would need a new agency decision and no binding mechanism is shown.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Well-supported-chain LA fails; not line-drawing.

error_sentence: Forty seconds is a long way from Armageddon
conditions_met_evidence: Rebuts the opponents' quoted hyperbole with pilot data; quote given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Rebutting a version someone really holds, saying whose.

error_sentence: flagged 93% ... versus 81% for the old system, with no increase in false alarms
conditions_met_evidence: C2 fails: evidence of improvement given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Newness plus evidence LA.
notes: Contrast with R016.

conditions_met_evidence: No argument: recipe.

error_sentence: So when the man at the next table collapsed, I was right not to call out for help. Rules are rules.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 silence rule applied. C2 a medical emergency, where the rule's purpose (undisturbed work) does not apply. C3 conclusion relies on applying it anyway.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Applying strictly for a stated reason' fails: 'Rules are rules' is a stock phrase, not a reason such as fairness considered against the exception.
notes: 'Rules are rules' could also be tagged thought-terminating cliche; not a separate error (same step).

error_sentence: A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.
conditions_met_evidence: No fallacy; epistemological exposition.
notes: Hume, Enquiry sec. 10 (historical).

error_sentence: with a margin of error of plus or minus 0.9 points
conditions_met_evidence: Precise figure with margin of error from a large probability sample.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Fake-precision LA (estimate with margin of error).

error_sentence: So at least some of this year's medal winners will have been exempted from the oral exam. As always, the final is graded out of 100.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 premises universal ('every student who scores above 100'). C2 conclusion existential ('at least some'). C3 context shows the class is empty: the final is graded out of 100.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Non-empty-class LA fails (the opposite is shown).

conditions_met_evidence: No argument: product description.

error_sentence: If the experts can't even agree with each other, nobody really knows whether salt affects blood pressure. So I'm not going to worry about how much I eat.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 experts disagree on the target (1,500 vs 2,300 mg). C2 concluded nobody knows whether salt affects blood pressure at all.
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'Concluding the specific disputed point is unsettled' fails: conclusion goes beyond the disputed point (contrast R037).

error_sentence: I found long-division drills soothing when I was a kid ... So when my third-graders sit through forty minutes of drills, they're feeling that same calm focus.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 teacher describes students' experience. C2 (outside-text, settled by text) the teacher's own childhood experience is attributed to them. C3 the conclusion depends on it.

error_sentence: The fidgeting and tears must be about something going on at home.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 the claim (they feel calm) faces counterevidence: fidgeting and tears. C2 extra assumption: trouble at home. C3 no independent reason; 'must' offered as settling.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Rescuing assumption has no support.
notes: Separate error from the projection step.

error_sentence: clause 2 defines "in the unit" as "kept or housed on the premises,"
conditions_met_evidence: Ambiguity acknowledged and resolved from the document's own definitions and heading.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Only one reading plausible in context once clause 2 is applied.
notes: Contrast with R062.

error_sentence: while the law may be sometimes hard for the individual, it is best for the race, because it insures the survival of the fittest in every department.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 evolutionary wording ('survival of the fittest', 'the law'). C2 offered as reason it is good ('best for the race'). C3 partly: what 'fittest' stands for is not spelled out; but a strongest reading (competition selects the most efficient businesses, which drives progress) is a substantive economic claim.
lookalikes_ruled_out: The economic-efficiency reading is plausible from 'in every department', so not flagged.
notes: Carnegie, 'Wealth' / Gospel of Wealth (historical). Also: 'It is here; we cannot evade it; no substitutes have been found' -> 'welcome ... as beneficial' moves from inevitability to approval; no catalog entry (see NOTES). Settled by whether 'fittest' means 'best' or only 'survives competition'.

error_sentence: The county's own records show construction contracts running from March 1881 to May 1882
conditions_met_evidence: Documentary evidence rebuts a legend; no condition met.

error_sentence: So the original quarantine period really was forty days, even though today the word covers isolation of any length.
conditions_met_evidence: Conclusion is about the original practice, supported by records; current meaning acknowledged.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Etymology explaining how a meaning arose.

error_sentence: They might as well accuse us of wishing men not to eat, because we object to the cultivation of corn by the State.
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker correctly identifies a false dilemma / misrepresentation and rebuts by parallel absurdity.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Correct use; fair reduction to absurdity.
notes: Bastiat, The Law (historical).

error_sentence: So the loaded pallet weighs at least 1,220 kilograms
One speaker called the proposal "the end of the district as we know it."
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: news report quoting a speaker.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Reporting (METHOD g).

error_sentence: I drew the boundaries around where the cases were thickest, and the factory upwind of that area opened in 2015. Resident: So the factory is causing cancer in our neighborhood.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 cluster boundaries drawn after seeing the cases (stated). C2 treated as evidence of a cause ('the factory is causing cancer'). C3 (outside-text, settled by text) no allowance for the hundreds of possible areas; no prior prediction.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not a lead to test: asserts a cause. Not cherry-picking (pattern search).
notes: Committed by Resident; Health officer correctly rebuts and investigates anyway (no issue). The factory attribution (timing/upwind) is the causal claim inside C2, not separately rowed.

error_sentence: So we'll rank agents purely on calls closed. Since unresolved problems can't be quantified, they don't really matter for judging the team.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 ranking purely on calls closed. C2 (outside-text) whether problems get solved is important to support work: common knowledge. C3 dismissed because hard to measure.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Measured thing is not the thing that matters.
notes: Contested-status entry (noted). Contrast with R035.

error_sentence: That came to 18,437 attendees. So we can tell the press that exactly 18,437 people turned up, not 18,000 or 19,000.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 five-figure precision from a ten-second one-corner count scaled up. C2 the precision is used to make the claim more authoritative ('exactly ... not 18,000 or 19,000').
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not an exact count; no margin of error.

error_sentence: Our volunteers counted the people in one corner of the square for ten seconds and multiplied by the area of the whole square.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 whole-square figure from one corner. C2 (outside-text) crowd density in a corner likely differs from the square as a whole: plausible, but not shown in the text. C3 bears on the total.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No weighting or check against other areas.
notes: Settled by whether density was uniform across the square. The method is also garbled (a count, not a density, multiplied by area); see other errors.

error_sentence: Hint: compare what Ana actually proposed with what Ben responds to.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: exercise that teaches straw man.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Teaching.

error_sentence: that counterfeit logic which presumes that because I did not want a negro woman for a slave, I do necessarily want her for a wife
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker correctly identifies a false dilemma.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Correct use (METHOD g).
notes: Lincoln, 1857 Springfield speech on Dred Scott (historical). The racist premise ('as God made us separate') is a moral and factual claim, not one of the catalog's reasoning errors; recorded for transparency.

error_sentence: All licensed electricians in this county are union members. Therefore all union members in this county have passed a safety exam.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 categorical syllogism. C2 minor term 'union members' distributed in the conclusion ('all union members'). C3 undistributed in the minor premise ('All licensed electricians ... are union members').
notes: Contrast with R020.

error_sentence: The most vulgar form of this fallacy is that which is commonly called post hoc, ergo propter hoc
conditions_met_evidence: No argument committed: Mill explains post hoc / cum hoc with examples.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Teaching.
notes: J. S. Mill, System of Logic bk 5 (historical).

error_sentence: That is a ridiculous notion, frankly absurd on its face. I'm not going to waste the council's time refuting nonsense.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 claim (fees will hurt shops) dismissed as absurd and not worth discussing. C2 no reason given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Not a pointer to a prior refutation; not mockery for a laugh (so not appeal to ridicule).

error_sentence: Every other component checked out, the failure was logged at the same second the outage began, and replacing that transformer restored power
conditions_met_evidence: Timing plus mechanism plus intervention; alternatives ruled out.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Post-hoc LA: timing plus mechanism or intervention.

error_sentence: Then he is a father, and he is yours; ergo, he is your father, and the puppies are your brothers.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 'father' and 'yours' are true separately (a father of puppies; owned by you) and are read as one unit, 'your father'. C2 the combined meaning gives the conclusion.
notes: Plato, Euthydemus (historical). Committed by the sophist in the dialogue; Plato's purpose is satire, so an author-level verdict would be no issue. Flagged at speaker level for consistency with the other multi-speaker items. Label disputed: Aristotle may treat this example under accident (accident-aristotle) rather than combination of words; see NOTES.

error_sentence: Last spring the district picked out the ten schools with the lowest reading scores ... This spring, eight of those ten schools improved. The program clearly works
conditions_met_evidence: C1 (outside-text, settled by text) schools selected for extreme low scores, followed by more ordinary scores. C2 program credited. C3 drift to average not considered; no comparison group.
lookalikes_ruled_out: No comparison group LA (contrast R038).
notes: Causation family order mentions 'reason cases were selected' under common cause; regression fallacy is the more specific entry for selection on an extreme. 'Rolled out statewide' from 10 schools is part of the same step.
